name: Te Waikoropupū Springs
summary: One of the clearest freshwater springs in the world.
detail: The easy loop leads to viewing platforms over the springs, but contact with the water is prohibited to protect its exceptional clarity and cultural significance. Allow time to read the interpretation panels and stay on the formed track. It pairs well with the nearby Pupu Hydro Walkway, though the two walks have separate access points.

name: Abel Tasman National Park
summary: Kayaking, hiking, and boat trips in paradise.
detail: Golden Bay visitors can approach the park from Wainui or drive the winding final section to Tōtaranui for beaches and day walks. Some Coast Track sections have tidal crossings, so check the tide timetable before choosing a route. Water taxis and guided trips are busiest in summer and are worth arranging before the day.

name: Pupu Hydro Walkway
summary: Scenic forest loop following an old hydro power scheme.
detail: This is a more demanding outing than the nearby springs walk, with a steady climb and narrow sections beside the historic water race. Wear shoes with good grip because roots and shaded surfaces can stay slick after rain. Set aside a few hours and visit Te Waikoropupū Springs separately rather than expecting the tracks to connect.

name: Aroha Health Spa
summary: Treat yourself — massage, facials, and holistic wellness experiences.
detail: Reserve a treatment ahead during holiday periods rather than relying on a same-day space. Confirm the current treatment menu and arrival instructions directly before travelling, as availability can vary. Its Takaka location makes a spa appointment easy to combine with lunch or gallery browsing in town.

name: Milnthorpe Park
summary: Explore over 13 km of walking tracks through regenerating forest.
detail: The network offers several route lengths, so check the entrance map and choose a loop that fits the daylight available. Forest sections can be muddy after rain, making covered footwear useful even on a short wander. Milnthorpe is a convenient nature stop while travelling between Collingwood and the western side of Golden Bay.

name: Hack Farm
summary: Guided beach horse rides near Patons Rock, suited to riders of all abilities.
detail: Ride times depend on conditions and the beach tide, so book ahead and reconfirm the departure details. Give the operator accurate rider ages and experience levels so they can prepare suitable horses and guidance. A Patons Rock holiday home keeps the early start or post-ride return especially simple.

name: Golden Bay Kayaks
summary: Rent kayaks at the iconic Tata Beach.
detail: Conditions on the bay can change quickly, so check the wind forecast and follow the operator's route advice before launching. Summer sessions can fill early, particularly on calm mornings, making advance booking sensible. Staying at Tata Beach lets you reach the launch without a long drive and leaves time for a swim after paddling.

name: Artisans of Golden Bay
summary: Visit potters, weavers, painters and other local artists.
detail: This is a self-guided trail of studios rather than one venue, so select a few makers and plan a realistic driving route around the bay. Studio hours can be seasonal or by appointment, and checking before setting out avoids a closed-door visit. The trail works well between beach days, with clusters of stops around Takaka and the road toward Collingwood.

name: Golden Bay Museum
summary: Local history including Māori, colonial and natural exhibits.
detail: The museum provides useful context for the bay's early settlement, industries and natural environment before you explore farther afield. Check its current opening days outside the main summer period. Because the visit is compact and in Takaka, it combines easily with a café, cinema session or nearby galleries.

name: Monza Gallery
summary: Local art and exhibitions in Takaka.
detail: Exhibitions and work on display change, giving repeat visitors a fresh look at local and New Zealand artists. Check the gallery's current opening hours before making a dedicated trip, especially outside summer. Its town-centre setting makes it an easy addition to a slower Takaka shopping or café afternoon.

name: Golden Bay Air Scenic Flights
summary: Flights over Golden Bay and Abel Tasman.
detail: Scenic flights are weather dependent, so keep some flexibility in the itinerary and confirm conditions with the operator on the day. Routes and flight lengths vary, making it worth choosing the landscapes you most want to see when booking. Departing from Takaka also makes the flight straightforward to pair with a stay on the eastern side of the bay.

name: Anatoki Salmon
summary: Catch your own salmon, they prepare it for you on-site.
detail: Allow more time than a normal lunch stop because catching the fish comes before it is prepared for you. Opening days and kitchen arrangements can vary through the year, so check the current details before driving out. The inland setting makes this a useful change of pace when beach weather is uncertain.

name: The Grove Scenic Reserve
summary: Short, magical walk among limestone rock formations.
detail: The short track threads through limestone blocks and dense native vegetation, with roots and uneven rock underfoot. Shaded sections can remain slippery after wet weather, so wear secure footwear despite the modest distance. Its position between Takaka and Pōhara makes it easy to add before or after time at the beach.

name: Labyrinth Rocks Park
summary: Free natural rock maze for all ages.
detail: The informal paths weave among limestone formations, and younger children should stay close where the passages branch. Uneven ground and damp rock call for closed shoes after rain. As a short stop close to Takaka, it leaves plenty of time for another indoor or outdoor activity the same day.

name: The Village Theatre (Takaka)
summary: A charming boutique cinema showing new releases and indie films.
detail: The programme is smaller than a multiplex schedule, so check the session time before heading into town. Popular screenings can be busier on wet days and during school holidays. The central Takaka location makes dinner or coffee before the film easy to arrange.

name: Rock Climbing
summary: Discover over 220 bolted limestone routes ranging from easy slabs to challenging overhangs.
detail: Golden Bay climbing requires the right equipment, route knowledge and experience; newcomers should arrange an experienced partner or local instruction. Limestone is best approached in suitable dry conditions, and current access notes should be checked because some crags cross private land. Takaka is a practical base for reaching the main climbing areas while remaining close to supplies and rest-day options.

name: Rawhiti Cave Walk
summary: A challenging hike to a unique stalactite-covered cave entrance.
detail: The track climbs steeply over rough ground, making this a poor choice for casual footwear or a rushed schedule. Go in dry conditions when possible and carry water, as the effort is concentrated on the ascent. The formed route is about viewing the dramatic cave entrance, so follow all signs and do not disturb the fragile formations.

name: Wainui Falls Walk
summary: Short forest walk to a stunning waterfall.
detail: The forest route includes roots, rocks and a suspension bridge, so secure footwear and close supervision of children are important. Parking is in demand during peak summer hours, and an earlier start can make the visit quieter. The walk pairs naturally with Tata Beach or the northern edge of Abel Tasman National Park.

name: Farewell Spit Tours
summary: Eco tours of the world's longest natural sandbar.
detail: Departure times follow the tides rather than a fixed daily timetable, so use the time confirmed for your particular tour. The exposed spit can feel cool and windy even when Collingwood is mild, making layers, water and sun protection useful. Tours take a substantial part of the day, and staying in Collingwood reduces the driving around an early or late departure.

name: Wharariki Beach Walk
summary: Iconic beach with wind-sculpted rock formations and seal pups at low tide.
detail: Reach the beach on foot across farmland from the road-end car park and be ready for strong wind with little shelter. Low tide reveals more sand around the rock formations, but the surf and currents make this a place for caution rather than a routine swimming stop. Keep a generous distance from seals and check both the tide and weather before the drive.

name: Paula's Kitchen
summary: Come and try a fusion of flavours mixing local, international, healthy and tasty takeaway food at Collingwood Wharf.
detail: The wharf location makes this a convenient takeaway stop before or after exploring Collingwood's waterfront. Check the day's opening hours before relying on it for a meal, particularly outside the summer season. It also fits neatly around a Farewell Spit tour when the tide-based departure leaves a gap in the day.

name: The Wholemeal Cafe
summary: Serves wholesome meals, great coffee, and local flavour in a relaxed historic setting.
detail: Its central location makes it a practical meeting point while browsing Takaka's shops and galleries. Lunch periods can be busy during peak holiday weeks, so allow some flexibility if travelling with a group. Check current evening and winter hours before planning the rest of the day around a visit.

name: The Dangerous Kitchen
summary: A lively café serving great coffee and fresh, creative dishes in a relaxed atmosphere.
detail: This is an easy town stop after a morning walk or while stocking up in Takaka. Service times can differ between daytime and evening, so check the current schedule before choosing it for dinner. During summer, arriving outside the main meal rush can make a relaxed visit easier.

name: O'sha Eatery
summary: A welcoming restaurant offering authentic Thai flavors in a modern, relaxed setting.
detail: Plan it as a Takaka dining stop after returning from nearby walks or beaches. Confirm the current dinner nights and reserve ahead for a larger group during busy holiday periods. A town-based meal is also a useful wet-weather option without committing to a long drive around the bay.

name: Ratanui Lodge Restaurant
summary: Refined dining in a relaxed setting with fresh, seasonal flavors.
detail: Restaurant availability can follow lodge service and seasonal schedules, so booking and confirming the current menu is advisable. The Pōhara setting suits a special dinner after a day at the beach without returning to Takaka. Guests staying locally can keep the evening simple and avoid a longer cross-bay drive.

name: Nikau Cafe & Bar
summary: A cosy spot for great coffee, fresh food, and relaxed dining.
detail: Use the venue's latest online updates to confirm opening days, which can change outside the busiest visitor period. Its Takaka location works well for a coffee break between errands, galleries or short local walks. Travellers heading farther west can also stop here before the longer drive toward Collingwood.

name: Tinky's Tavern
summary: A friendly Collingwood pub serving hearty meals, cold drinks, and good vibes.
detail: This is a practical evening meal option after a day around Farewell Spit or Wharariki Beach. Check the kitchen's current serving hours if returning late from a tide-timed tour. Staying in Collingwood keeps the trip home short after dinner and avoids retracing the road toward Takaka.
